policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'into your synagogue' takes its possessive from the following genitive; the presence or absence of the article before synagogue leaves no trace in the English, and the only note is an alternative_rendering about the word 'synagogue'.
ASV opens the clause with 'and', which renders either the postpositive de of the base or the prefixed kai equally; the connective choice is not distinguished.
ASV renders the parallel dative in the same verse explicitly ('ye say to the poor man') but has no corresponding 'unto him' with the first 'and say'; the added auto has no English counterpart.
ASV attaches 'there' to the standing ('Stand thou there, or sit under my footstool'), which requires ekei before e kathou, and it has no 'here' for the sitting, excluding the reading that adds hode.
ASV begins the question with 'do ye not' and no connective, but an untranslated introductory kai is ordinary in the ASV; both notes are alternative_rendering and bear on English wording only.
ASV 'poor as to the world' renders a dative of reference; the genitive reading would yield 'the poor of the world', which the ASV does not have.
ASV 'whosoever shall keep ... and yet stumble' renders the aorist subjunctive and the future indicative alike, and the base's differing punctuation has no English counterpart.

ASV quotes the commandment as the prohibition 'Do not commit adultery' rather than the future 'Thou shalt not' it uses when rendering the future indicative at Ex. 20:13f., matching the aorist subjunctive.
ASV 'said also, Do not kill' is a prohibition, not the future 'Thou shalt not kill' of the Decalogue rendering, matching the aorist subjunctive.
ASV 'if thou dost not commit adultery, but killest' is present tense throughout; the future reading would give 'shalt not commit adultery ... shalt kill'.
Both forms stand as the subject of 'mercy glorieth against judgment'; the case ending of eleos leaves no trace in the English.
ASV 'What doth it profit' is an idiomatic rendering that the article before ophelos does not change.
ASV begins 'If a brother or sister' with no connective, but an untranslated de is ordinary in the ASV and does not distinguish the readings.
ASV 'be naked and in lack of daily food' supplies one copula for both members; an explicit osin would be rendered no differently.
ASV 'what doth it profit?' is unchanged by the article before ophelos.
ASV 'if it have not works' renders either order of eche and erga; the variant is word order only.
ASV 'show me thy faith apart from thy works' renders choris; ek would be 'by' or 'from', as the ASV renders it in the answering clause 'I by my works'.
ASV has 'apart from thy works' with 'thy' unitalicized, so the possessive answers to sou in the text rendered.
ASV 'will show thee my faith' fixes the English order regardless of whether soi precedes or follows deixo; the variant is word order only.
ASV has 'my faith' with 'my' unitalicized, answering to mou in the text rendered rather than to the bare article.

The mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read there is one God' puts the anarthrous reading in the margin, so the ASV text is not r01; between the two articular readings 'God is one' the word order is not distinguished.
ASV 'faith apart from works is barren' renders arge; nekra would be 'dead', as the ASV renders it in verses 17 and 26.
ASV 'Ye see that by works a man is justified' carries no inferential adverb; toinun is emphatic and would be rendered 'then' or 'therefore'.
ASV opens the verse 'For as the body', rendering gar; the reading that omits it leaves the English 'For' unaccounted for.
ASV 'apart from works' renders either the bare noun or the articular one, since Greek articles with abstract plurals are not represented in this ASV phrase.
